intro.data: A product bundles two things into one. A Record holds a Name and an Age together — and it comes with two projections to pull each part back out. Recover the Name.
intro.alchemy: A product bundles two things into one. A Compound holds Salt and Sulfur together — and it comes with two projections to pull each part back out. Recover the Salt.
intro.spellcraft: A product bundles two things into one. A Blend holds Light and Heat together — and it comes with two projections to pull each part back out. Recover the Light.
intro.abstract: A product A×B bundles two objects, with projections π₁ and π₂ to recover each. Recover A.

goal.data: Wire the Record through the projection that recovers the Name.
goal.alchemy: Wire the Compound through the projection that recovers the Salt.
goal.spellcraft: Wire the Blend through the projection that recovers the Light.
goal.abstract: Wire A×B through π₁ to reach A.

afterSuccess.data: The projection pulled the Name back out of the Record. A product always comes with two projections — getName and getAge — one for each part it bundles.
afterSuccess.alchemy: The projection pulled the Salt back out of the Compound. A product always comes with two projections, one for each part it bundles.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: The projection pulled the Light back out of the Blend. A product always comes with two projections, one for each part it bundles.
afterSuccess.abstract: π₁ recovered A from A×B. A product comes with two projections π₁, π₂ — one for each factor.

reveal.summary: A product A×B bundles two objects and provides projections π₁ : A×B → A and π₂ : A×B → B to read each component back out.
reveal.moreFormal: What makes A×B a product isn't just the projections — it's the universal property: any pair of maps into A and B factors uniquely through A×B. That's the next puzzle.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: record.name and record.age — a tuple with two accessors.
